_comment: House copy for the Observer. Each story kind has headlines and bodies; one of each is picked per edition. Placeholders in {braces} come from the news desk. The writing model's settings are in press.json. House style: a small-town paper that reports blocky everyday life with complete seriousness. Never cruel, never gory, suitable for all ages. 'tones': house templates for the Roast and the Chronicle, by story kind; any kind missing there uses 'stories'.

opinions.headline: Editorial: It Is Time We Talked About Gravel
opinions.body: Every resident has a gravel story. You dig up, it falls down. You dig across, it falls down anyway. The Observer does not ask for much. We ask only that gravel be held to the same standards as every other block, and stay where it is put.

opinions.headline: Opinion: Should Creepers Be Required to Knock?
opinions.body: Other visitors knock. Villagers mumble. Even zombies groan as they approach. The creeper alone arrives in perfect silence, hisses once, and redesigns your front wall. The Observer believes a simple knock would go a long way.

opinions.headline: Letters: A Reader Writes About the Moon
opinions.body: "Sir, I have noticed the moon is square. My mother noticed it, and her mother before her. Nobody else seems bothered. Am I alone?" The Observer replies: you are not alone, but you are outnumbered. We suggest admiring it anyway.

opinions.headline: Editorial: In Praise of the Humble Torch
opinions.body: It asks for a stick and a little coal. It lights the way, keeps the monsters at bay and never complains. This week the Observer raises a glass to the torch, the quiet hero of every mine shaft in the land.

opinions.headline: Opinion: The Case Against Leaving Doors Open
opinions.body: It takes no time at all to close a door, and yet open doors remain the town's greatest source of unexpected guests. The Observer does not wish to name names. The Observer simply notes that zombies cannot open iron ones.

opinions.headline: Advice Column: Ask the Editor
opinions.body: "Dear Editor, a villager keeps staring at me. What should I do?" Answer: Nothing. Villagers stare at everyone. It is how they show they care, or possibly how they decide what to charge you. Either way, smile and keep walking.

opinions.headline: Editorial: Why Do We Keep Building on Lava?
opinions.body: The Observer has lost count of the number of residents who have lost a full set of tools to a single careless step. Lava does not negotiate. Lava does not forgive. Lava, the Observer suggests, is best admired from a distance.

opinions.headline: Opinion: Let Us Be Kinder to Chickens
opinions.body: They lay eggs without being asked. They wander harmlessly. They ask nothing of us but a little seed. And yet chickens remain the town's most overlooked residents. The Observer calls for a week of chicken appreciation.

opinions.headline: Letters: On the Subject of Beds
opinions.body: "Sir, I put my bed in the Nether to save time and it went badly. Should I have been warned?" The Observer replies: you are now warned, as are all our readers. Beds belong in the Overworld, and nowhere else.

opinions.headline: Editorial: A Modest Proposal Regarding Endermen
opinions.body: The Observer asks only this of our tall neighbours: if you must take a block, please take one from somewhere that is not the middle of somebody's house. We have also stopped looking them in the eye, which is helping.
